books.title: Project Hail Mary
books.author: Andy Weir
books.description: Ryland Grace wakes alone on a spacecraft with no memory and a mission that will decide the fate of Earth. Armed with improvised science and a stubborn streak, he finds that the strangest help comes from the most unlikely friend.
books.tagline: One astronaut, one impossible friendship.

reviews.text: Funny, tense and weirdly tender. The humor never gets in the way of the stakes, and the plot keeps surprising you.
The world building is wonderful and the pacing is relentless. I wanted a little more depth from the supporting cast.

books.title: The Song of Achilles
books.author: Madeline Miller
books.description: Patroclus, a quiet exiled prince, is drawn into the orbit of golden Achilles. Their friendship deepens into love as the shadow of the Trojan War closes in, in a retelling that is as tender as it is devastating.
books.tagline: A tender love story with a war closing in.

reviews.text: The prose is beautiful from the first page, and the relationship at the center is so tender that the ending broke me. A little slow in the middle, but I never wanted to stop.
Lyrical writing and deep characters. The pacing is measured, so give it time.

books.title: Klara and the Sun
books.author: Kazuo Ishiguro
books.description: Klara is an Artificial Friend who studies the world from a shop window, waiting for a child to choose her. Once she does, she watches over a fragile family and keeps faith in the power of the Sun.
books.tagline: A gentle machine watches over a fragile family.

reviews.text: Quiet, strange and moving. The writing is gorgeous, though the pacing is slow and some readers will want more plot.
A gentle book with a lot of heart. Klara is a wonderful narrator and the ending stayed with me.

books.title: The Midnight Library
books.author: Matt Haig
books.description: Between life and death, Nora Seed finds a library where every book is a life she could have lived. She sets out to find the one worth keeping.
books.tagline: Every life you could have lived, on a shelf.

books.title: Tomorrow, and Tomorrow, and Tomorrow
books.author: Gabrielle Zevin
books.description: Two childhood friends reunite in college and begin building video games together. Over three decades of ambition, rivalry and grief, the games become the place where they love each other best.
books.tagline: Two friends, three decades, one game.

reviews.text: The friendship at the center is the best I have read in years. Sharp dialogue, funny in places and devastating in others.
Emotional and clever. The game design details never feel heavy, and the characters are unforgettable.

books.title: The Silent Patient
books.author: Alex Michaelides
books.description: Alicia Berenson shot her husband and has not spoken since. Theo Faber, a psychotherapist, is determined to make her talk, and to find out what really happened.
books.tagline: A woman who will not speak, a man who must know.

books.title: Atomic Habits
books.author: James Clear
books.description: A practical guide to building good habits and breaking bad ones. Clear argues that small changes, repeated every day, compound into remarkable results.
books.tagline: Tiny changes, remarkable results.

books.title: Norwegian Wood
books.author: Haruki Murakami
books.description: Toru Watanabe looks back on the 1960s and on the fragile, luminous Naoko, whom he loved. A coming-of-age story about grief, desire and learning to stay alive.
books.tagline: Memory, grief and a quiet kind of love.

books.title: The Alchemist
books.author: Paulo Coelho
books.description: Santiago, an Andalusian shepherd boy, follows a recurring dream to the Egyptian pyramids. On the road he learns to read the signs the world leaves for those who listen.
books.tagline: A shepherd follows a dream to the pyramids.

books.author: George Orwell
books.description: Winston Smith works rewriting history for a Party that watches everything. His small, secret acts of rebellion lead him toward a love, and a reckoning, he cannot escape.
books.tagline: A world where the Party controls the past.

books.title: The Seven Husbands of Evelyn Hugo
books.author: Taylor Jenkins Reid
books.description: Reclusive Hollywood icon Evelyn Hugo finally agrees to tell her story to an unknown journalist. Seven marriages later, the truth about the love of her life is waiting.
books.tagline: Seven marriages, one great love.

books.title: A Man Called Ove
books.author: Fredrik Backman
books.description: Ove is a grumpy widower with firm opinions about parking and a plan to end his life. New neighbours keep getting in the way, and slowly bring him back to the living.
books.tagline: A grumpy man who is not done living.

books.title: The Martian
books.author: Andy Weir
books.description: Stranded on Mars after a dust storm forces his crew to flee, botanist Mark Watney has to science his way to survival. With wit as sharp as his math, he turns every problem into a plan.
books.tagline: Alone on Mars with duct tape and math.

reviews.text: So funny and so tense. The plot is a puzzle with a great voice, though the characters are lighter than in Project Hail Mary.

books.title: Circe
books.author: Madeline Miller
books.description: Banished to a remote island, the witch Circe hones her craft among gods, monsters and mortals. A retelling of the Odyssey told with patience and fire.
books.tagline: A witch, an island, and the gods at her door.

reviews.text: The prose is gorgeous and Circe is a wonderful character. The pacing is slow in places, but the world is so vivid that I kept reading.
Lyrical, patient and emotional. A beautiful retelling.

books.title: Never Let Me Go
books.author: Kazuo Ishiguro
books.description: Kathy looks back on her years at Hailsham, a boarding school with a strange purpose, and on her friendships with Ruth and Tommy. A quiet novel that hurts for a long time.
books.tagline: A quiet novel that hurts for a long time.

reviews.text: Quiet, haunting and heartbreaking. The pacing is slow, but the writing is superb and the ending hurts.

books.title: Anxious People
books.author: Fredrik Backman
books.description: A failed bank robber takes a group of strangers hostage at an apartment viewing. As the standoff unravels, each of them reveals the small sadnesses they carry.
books.tagline: A hostage situation with a lot of heart.

reviews.text: Hilarious and moving. The dialogue is sharp and the characters feel like people you know.

books.title: Beartown
books.author: Fredrik Backman
books.description: In a failing forest town, hope rests on a junior ice hockey team. When a shocking event divides the community, everyone must decide what they are willing to protect.
books.tagline: A town, a team, and a choice.

books.title: Daisy Jones & The Six
books.author: Taylor Jenkins Reid
books.description: An oral history of a 1970s rock band that rose too fast and broke up at the height of its fame. Everyone remembers the story differently.
books.tagline: A rock band, told in many voices.

books.title: Piranesi
books.author: Susanna Clarke
books.description: Piranesi lives in a vast house of endless halls, statues and tides. His journals record a gentle life of exploration, until messages begin to appear that suggest he is not alone.
books.tagline: A house with endless halls and a secret.

reviews.text: The world building is extraordinary and the writing is hypnotic. Short, strange and perfectly edited.
Atmospheric and beautifully written. The characters are sparse, which suits the story, and the ending is satisfying.

books.title: Legends & Lattes
books.author: Travis Baldree
books.description: Viv, a retired orc mercenary, hangs up her sword to open the first coffee shop in the city of Thune. A low-stakes tale about found family and very good coffee.
books.tagline: Swords down, coffee up.

reviews.text: The coziest book I have read in ages. Light, funny and heartwarming, with characters I wanted to keep.

books.title: The House in the Cerulean Sea
books.author: TJ Klune
books.description: A caseworker for magical youth is sent to inspect an orphanage on a remote island. Six unusual children and their mysterious guardian change everything he thought he knew.
books.tagline: A strange orphanage on a faraway island.

books.title: Station Eleven
books.author: Emily St. John Mandel
books.description: A flu pandemic ends the modern world. Twenty years on, a travelling Shakespeare company moves through a changed landscape, held together by art and memory.
books.tagline: After the collapse, the art goes on.

reviews.text: Beautifully written and haunting. The structure is layered, and the ending is quietly hopeful.

books.title: A Gentleman in Moscow
books.author: Amor Towles
books.description: In 1922 Count Rostov is sentenced to house arrest in a grand Moscow hotel. Confined to its rooms, he finds a larger life than he ever expected.
books.tagline: A count, a hotel, a whole life.

reviews.text: Charming, witty and warm. The prose is a joy and the characters are wonderful.

books.title: The Night Circus
books.author: Erin Morgenstern
books.description: Le Cirque des Rêves arrives without warning and opens only at night. Within its black and white tents, two young magicians are locked in a contest neither of them chose.
books.tagline: A circus that arrives without warning.

books.title: Kafka on the Shore
books.author: Haruki Murakami
books.description: A teenage runaway and an aging man who talks to cats travel on parallel paths. Dreams, prophecies and a small private library pull them toward the same place.
books.tagline: Two journeys, one strange destiny.

books.title: Small Things Like These
books.author: Claire Keegan
books.description: Bill Furlong, a coal merchant in 1985 Ireland, makes a discovery at the local convent. One quiet decision tests what he owes to other people.
books.tagline: One quiet decision in a small town.

reviews.text: Tiny and perfect. The writing is spare, the editing is flawless, and the emotional weight is huge.

books.title: The Secret History
books.author: Donna Tartt
books.description: At a small Vermont college, a group of Classics students falls under the spell of their charismatic professor. A murder is only the beginning of what they will cover up.
books.tagline: Classics students and a shared secret.

books.title: Dune
books.author: Frank Herbert
books.description: On the desert planet Arrakis, young Paul Atreides inherits a dangerous fate. Politics, ecology and prophecy converge around the spice that powers the empire.
books.tagline: Power, prophecy and a planet of sand.

reviews.text: The world building is unmatched. It is dense and complex, and the pacing is slow at first, but it rewards patience.

books.title: The Road
books.author: Cormac McCarthy
books.description: A father and his young son walk through a burned America, carrying fire and little else. A spare, devastating story about what it means to keep going.
books.tagline: A father, a son, and the road.

reviews.text: Bleak and beautiful. The prose is spare and the tone is relentlessly dark, so it is not an easy read.

books.title: Pachinko
books.author: Min Jin Lee
books.description: Four generations of a Korean family make a life in Japan, facing prejudice with grit. A sweeping story of survival, shame and quiet love.
books.tagline: Four generations, two countries, one family.

reviews.text: Sweeping and deeply moving. The characters stay with you, and the world feels real. The pacing is slow, but it is worth it.

books.title: Convenience Store Woman
books.author: Sayaka Murata
books.description: Keiko has worked at the same convenience store for eighteen years and feels most herself there. Pressure to live a more normal life arrives in the form of an unlikely new coworker.
books.tagline: A woman who belongs in the shop.

books.title: Stoner
books.author: John Williams
books.description: William Stoner, the son of a farmer, discovers a love of literature and spends his life as a university teacher. A quiet novel about work, love and what a life amounts to.
books.tagline: A quiet life, fully seen.

books.title: The Long Way to a Small, Angry Planet
books.author: Becky Chambers
books.description: Rosemary joins the crew of the Wayfarer, a patched-together ship that punches tunnels through space. Between jobs, the oddball crew becomes the family she never had.
books.tagline: A found family crosses the galaxy.

books.title: A Psalm for the Wild-Built
books.author: Becky Chambers
books.description: Sibling Dex leaves city life to travel the countryside as a tea monk, serving comfort to small towns. Then a robot, long thought a myth, steps out of the woods and asks what people need.
books.tagline: A tea monk and a robot meet in the woods.

books.title: Hamnet
books.author: Maggie O'Farrell
books.description: In Elizabethan England, a quiet Warwickshire family is shaken by the sickness that takes their young son. A luminous imagining of the grief that may have shaped one of the most famous plays ever written.
books.tagline: A family, a plague, and a play.

books.title: All the Light We Cannot See
books.author: Anthony Doerr
books.description: A blind French girl and a gifted German boy move toward each other through occupied Europe. Radio waves, a hidden jewel and a city under bombardment connect their separate lives.
books.tagline: Two young lives on opposite sides of a war.

books.title: Eleanor Oliphant Is Completely Fine
books.author: Gail Honeyman
books.description: Eleanor Oliphant likes her routines, her vodka on the weekend and her own company. One small act of kindness and one very ordinary man start to crack the careful life she has built.
books.tagline: Completely fine, thank you very much.

books.title: The Book Thief
books.author: Markus Zusak
books.description: In Nazi Germany, Liesel Meminger steals books and shares them with the neighbours sheltering in a basement. Narrated by Death, it is a story about words and the small mercies that survive a war.
books.tagline: Death narrates a girl who steals books.

books.title: Normal People
books.author: Sally Rooney
books.description: Connell and Marianne grow up in the same small town in Ireland, one popular and one an outsider. Through school and university, their lives circle and collide in ways neither can quite say out loud.
books.tagline: Two people, years of almost.

books.title: A Little Life
books.author: Hanya Yanagihara
books.description: Four friends move to New York after college and build their lives together over decades. At the center is Jude, whose past shapes everything in an immersive, harrowing story about friendship and endurance.
books.tagline: Four friends, one long and painful love.

books.title: The Fellowship of the Ring
books.author: J.R.R. Tolkien
books.description: A quiet hobbit inherits a ring that the whole world wants, and leaves home with a few friends to carry it somewhere it can be unmade.
books.tagline: One small burden, one very long road.

books.title: The Two Towers
books.author: J.R.R. Tolkien
books.description: The fellowship is broken. Its scattered members face war in the west while two hobbits press on toward the shadowed land.
books.tagline: The company is scattered; the road goes on.

books.title: The Return of the King
books.author: J.R.R. Tolkien
books.description: Armies gather at the last free city while the ring-bearer makes his way through the land he has dreaded all along.
books.tagline: Every road ends somewhere.
